title: Visual Studio Code on Linux saves this document by truncating and rewriting the same object

provenance.fixture: Before each run, <root>/doc.txt contained exactly `alpha original document\n`. The pinned official arm64 Debian package ran under Xvfb with network disabled. The driver opened that file in a fresh VS Code profile, discovered that owned child through its OS-assigned loopback DevToolsActivePort, validated the real document editor, typed `VS Code edit: `, invoked Ctrl-S and rejected any final bytes other than `VS Code edit: alpha original document\n`.
provenance.evidence: Four independent fresh-profile runs exited 0 in 3.27 s, 3.54 s, 3.49 s and 3.61 s. Every run kept `doc.txt` at inode 255 and changed 24 bytes to 38 exact bytes. One run observed the SAME inode at 0 bytes between them; three polling runs saw 24 -> 38 directly. No temporary path appeared in any reading. The fourth run used an image built from the checked-in editor-artifact-pinned rebuild recipe.
provenance.surprise: The Linux result agrees with the real macOS document-save path rather than the older atomic-write binary derivation. The transient empty state was visible in one of four Linux runs, demonstrating both the in-place truncate hazard and the polling backend's admissible omission of that intermediate state.
blind_spots: open, flush, fsync and close are invisible to polling
three of four runs completed truncation and rewrite between readings
a temporary created and removed entirely between two readings would be missed, but the unchanged inode proves that no temporary replaced doc.txt

objects.role: doc.txt, the document — one identity throughout

folder.fidelity: a backend that does not declare ObserveDurableBoundary
folder.omission_note: Three of four runs observed exactly this omission: truncation and rewrite completed between readings, so the folder view saw one Written. The run that caught both writes proves the skipped state can be an unsafe empty document.

expected.meaningful_durable_change: doc.txt holds the exact edited text in the same object identity. The zero-length intermediate state is not a meaningful save.
expected.forbidden_note: Mount sequence 2 and folder sequence 1 are the zero-length state observed in one repetition. A checkpoint there would turn one ordinary VS Code save into a durable empty document; the two omitted observations do not make that state safe.

notes: The official package and every dependency were downloaded while building the image; the editor package alone is checksum pinned, and the four actual editor captures ran with Docker network disabled.
On a mount, Closed anchors the meaningful boundary. On a folder backend, only established settling can close the window after the rewrite.
